# Biodiversity — genetic, species, and ecosystem levels

## 1. Introduction
Opening frame for **Biodiversity — genetic** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Biodiversity and Conservation fill pass.

## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Biodiversity — genetic
### species
### and ecosystem levels

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

**Biodiversity** is the totality of variation in life, measured at three nested levels: **genetic** (variation within a species — rice varieties, dog breeds), **species** (the variety of species in a region) and **ecosystem** (the variety of habitats — Terai grassland, hill forest, alpine meadow). It is the outcome of ~3.5 billion years of evolution, and it is currently being lost faster than at any time since the dinosaurs.

**Concept flow — the three levels, nested (study in this order)**

| Step | Level | Measured as | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Genetic diversity | Allele and gene variants within one species | 2000+ traditional rice varieties; local buffalo breeds |
| 2 | Species diversity | Species richness + evenness in a community | ~8.7 million eukaryote species estimated; Nepal ~2% of flowering plants of the world |
| 3 | Ecosystem diversity | Variety of habitats and communities in a region | Terai jungle → mid-hill forest → alpine meadow within 200 km in Nepal |
| 4 | Why it matters | Ecosystem services: food, medicine, pollination, water, climate regulation | Loss of one level undermines the ones above it |

**Why biodiversity matters — services classified**

| Service type | Examples | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Provisioning | Food, timber, fibres, medicines (many from plants, e.g. alkaloids) | Species are raw material |
| Regulating | Pollination, flood control, water purification, climate regulation | Ecosystems process flows |
| Supporting | Soil formation, nutrient cycling, primary production | Underlies all other services |
| Cultural | Aesthetic, spiritual, ecotourism values | Human relationship with nature |
| Option value | Future unknown uses — new drugs, new crops | Genetic diversity is the bank |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — one gene that mattered.** In the 1970s, rice crops across Asia were threatened by grassy stunt virus. Breeders screened thousands of varieties and found resistance in one wild relative, *Oryza nivara* — a single population from a single place. That gene now protects millions of hectares. Every wild population is an unopened safety deposit box: genetic diversity is insurance we usually only notice when the disaster arrives.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Three levels with examples: genetic (rice varieties, 50,000+ strains), species (India: ~45,000 plants, 90,000+ animals), ecosystem (forests, wetlands, coral reefs) — one example each.
Trick 2: Latitudinal gradient: species richness ↑ toward the tropics — three hypotheses: speciation time (stable climate), productivity, niche specialisation.
Trick 3: Species–area relation: log S = log C + Z log A; Z ≈ 0.1–0.2 mainland, 0.3–1.5 islands — the equation is the standard 2-marker.
Trick 4: India's status: mega-diverse country, 3 of 34 biodiversity hotspots (Western Ghats, Eastern Himalaya, Indo-Burma).
